abstention.detail: The file compiles, but declaration_search reports pre-existing declarations named `Meromorphic.add/mul/deriv` in the base corpus (likely from other namespaces or packages), and I could not confirm from tool output whether these are genuine name collisions affecting Mathlib’s namespace resolution.

Searched Mathlib for an existing global predicate `Meromorphic` and for existing simp lemma `MeromorphicOn f Set.univ ↔ ...` plus closure lemmas; only the new additions in `Analysis/Meromorphic/Basic.lean` matched, and the remaining lemmas are just pointwise wrappers around existing `MeromorphicAt` lemmas rather than duplicating separate global API.

Checked the new `Meromorphic` shorthand and its basic API lemmas (`add/sub/mul/div/pow/zpow/deriv` plus `fun_*` and `Finset` sum/prod variants) for missing expected counterparts or obvious generalisations (e.g. to `MeromorphicOn`/`SetLike`-style, or non-univ sets); this set looks consistent with the intended `MeromorphicOn _ Set.univ` abbreviation and the Zulip guidance.

candidates.claim: The declaration name `Meromorphic.add` collides with several pre-existing `Meromorphic.add` declarations from dependencies, so adding this lemma under `namespace Meromorphic` creates an ambiguous/noncanonical API name and risks import-order breakage.
candidates.requested_change: Rename the namespace for the new predicate API (e.g. `namespace MeromorphicFn` or `namespace Meromorphic` -> `namespace Meromorphic` with lemma names prefixed like `Meromorphic_add` at top level), or rename the lemma to avoid the globally-colliding identifier `Meromorphic.add`.
candidates.suggested_fix: A common pattern is to avoid a bare namespace matching a predicate name when that name is already used elsewhere; alternatively keep the namespace but use a different lemma name such as `Meromorphic.add'` is not acceptable—prefer `Meromorphic.add_`-style only if existing; otherwise move lemmas to a different namespace.

abstention.detail: Ran `naming_norm` on all 24 new declarations (`Meromorphic`, `meromorphicOn_univ`, and the `Meromorphic.*` lemmas); each returned `insufficient_evidence`, and I found no maintainer precedent to justify a naming request anyway.

candidates.claim: In `meromorphicOn_univ`, the statement has an extra space before `:=` and an extra space before the line break: `MeromorphicOn f Set.univ ↔ Meromorphic f  := by tauto`. This deviates from the file's otherwise consistent spacing and multi-line `by` formatting used nearby.
candidates.concern_label: extra spaces and one-line `by` proof formatting

proposed_edit.replacement:
/-- A function is meromorphic iff it is meromorphic on `Set.univ`. -/
@[simp]
lemma meromorphicOn_univ {f : 𝕜 → E} : MeromorphicOn f Set.univ ↔ Meromorphic f := by
  tauto

candidates.requested_change: Remove the double space before `:=`, and format the `by` proof on the next line (optionally with backticks around `Set.univ` in the docstring, matching common style).

candidates.claim: In `Meromorphic.fun_neg`, the term has an extra space before the closing parenthesis: `Meromorphic (fun x ↦ -f x )`. This is inconsistent with surrounding lambdas in the same section (e.g. `fun x ↦ f x + g x`).
candidates.concern_label: space before closing paren in lambda

proposed_edit.replacement:
@[fun_prop]
lemma fun_neg (hf : Meromorphic f) : Meromorphic (fun x ↦ -f x) := hf.neg

candidates.requested_change: Remove the stray space before `)` in the lambda expression.

candidates.claim: `Meromorphic.pow` is on a single long line: `lemma pow ... : Meromorphic (f ^ n) := fun x ↦ ...`. In this file, multi-argument lemmas are typically broken so that the proof starts on a new line after `:=` (see e.g. `add`, `sub`, etc.).

proposed_edit.replacement:
@[fun_prop]
lemma pow {f : 𝕜 → 𝕜} {n : ℕ} (hf : Meromorphic f) : Meromorphic (f ^ n) :=
  fun x ↦ (hf x).pow n

candidates.requested_change: Reformat `Meromorphic.pow` to put the proof term on the next line, indented.

candidates.claim: `Meromorphic.zpow` is on a single long line: `lemma zpow ... : Meromorphic (f ^ n) := fun x ↦ ...`. Nearby lemmas in this namespace break after `:=` when the right-hand side is nontrivial.

proposed_edit.replacement:
@[fun_prop]
lemma zpow {f : 𝕜 → 𝕜} {n : ℤ} (hf : Meromorphic f) : Meromorphic (f ^ n) :=
  fun x ↦ (hf x).zpow n

candidates.requested_change: Reformat `Meromorphic.zpow` to put the proof term on the next line, indented.

candidates.claim: `Meromorphic.deriv` is on a single long line: `lemma deriv ... : Meromorphic (deriv f) := fun x ↦ ...`. In the surrounding block, similar lemmas with a `fun x ↦ ...` RHS are formatted with the RHS on the next line (e.g. `add`, `sub`, `mul`, `div`).

proposed_edit.replacement:
@[fun_prop]
lemma deriv [CompleteSpace E] (hf : Meromorphic f) : Meromorphic (deriv f) :=
  fun x ↦ (hf x).deriv

candidates.requested_change: Reformat `Meromorphic.deriv` to put the proof term on the next line, indented.
